SEBoK Performance-Based Management, Distilled

Fifth-batch SEBoK distillation, batch 1 of 5 (SE-167). Target page is 404; the canonical carrier is Measurement (cross-referenced through Systems Engineering and Project Management). Performance-based management is dispersed across Measurement (the four-activity measurement process and the MOE/MOP/TPM technical-measure trichotomy), the project-management knowledge area (which lists EVM-adjacent topics), and external standards (PSM, GQM, ISO/IEC/IEEE 15939). Cluster J D8 dispersed-instrument with D8.1 external-carrier sub-pattern co-present (the EVM rung lives in PMI's PMBOK and the practical-measurement rung in PSM/ISO 15939). The Measurement page supplies the structural readings: a four-activity ordinal-axis lattice (Establish Commitment / Plan / Perform / Evaluate), a three-instance MOE/MOP/TPM technical-measure lattice, a three-carrier robustness instance (PSM / GQM / ISO 15939), and a four-pitfall hypostatic-boundary teaching cluster (golden-measure / single-pass / data-without-information-need / inappropriate-use). SE-167 is the dedicated stress-test for the paired-parallel-lattice Cluster A sub-form first proposed at SE-135 MBSE (Properties × Criteria as twin N=10 lattices co-bound at the modeling rung). SE-167 surfaces a second paired-parallel-lattice instance: the four-activity measurement process and the three-MOE/MOP/TPM technical-measure trichotomy are co-bound at the measurement-engagement rung — the four-activity process IS the procedural lattice within which the three-measure-type lattice is operationalized. Two-axis paired-parallel-lattice second confirming instance. Seven clusters compose.

II. Source Read

The target page does not exist. Measurement is the canonical carrier for performance-based management content within SEBoK. Measurement and analysis are "fundamental elements of systems engineering and technical management," providing information about products, services, and processes to support effective management and objective quality evaluation. The four-activity measurement process: Establish and Sustain Commitment (resources, training, management buy-in), Plan Measurement (define measures aligned with decision-makers' information needs), Perform Measurement (collect, prepare, analyze, present), Evaluate Measurement (assess relevance to business goals). Three frameworks: PSM (Practical Software and Systems Measurement, information categories and measurable concepts), GQM (Goal Question Metric), ISO/IEC/IEEE 15939 (international standard). Three technical-measure types: MOEs (Measures of Effectiveness — how well the system meets mission needs), MOPs (Measures of Performance — how well system components function), TPMs (Technical Performance Measures — track specific attributes throughout development). Leading indicators "provide visibility into expected project performance and potential future states." Four critical pitfalls: golden measures, single-pass, data-without-information-need, inappropriate-use. The Systems Engineering and Project Management knowledge area indexes performance-management-related topics (PMBOK, PM-SE relationship) but does not develop performance-based management as a standalone discipline.

III. Structural Read

Editorial-state observation. Cluster J D8 dispersed-instrument with D8.1 external-carrier sub-pattern co-present (paralleling SE-162's layered dispersion). Internal-migration: Measurement is the SEBoK carrier. External-carrier: EVM rung lives in PMI PMBOK; PSM and ISO 15939 carry the practical-measurement rung externally. Layered dispersion at moderate density.

Cluster A (universal-sibling lattice, Doc 572 Appendix D), paired-parallel-lattice second confirmed instance. SE-039 §VII.7 candidate refinement #10 named paired-parallel-lattice at SE-135 MBSE Process (Properties × Criteria as twin N=10 lattices co-bound at the modeling rung). SE-167 stress-tests this candidate. The Measurement carrier surfaces two co-bound lattices: (i) the four-activity measurement process (Establish Commitment / Plan / Perform / Evaluate) is universal-sibling at the measurement-engagement rung with ordinal-axis (D.5 sub-form); (ii) the three-measure-type trichotomy (MOE / MOP / TPM) is universal-sibling at the technical-measure rung with rung-axis (effectiveness rung / performance rung / development-tracking rung). The two lattices are paired-parallel: the four-activity process is the procedural lattice within which the three-measure-type lattice is operationalized; each measurement engagement instantiates BOTH lattices, with the procedural lattice as the sequencing dimension and the measure-type lattice as the discriminator-aspect dimension. Twin lattices co-bound at the measurement-engagement rung. SE-167 is the second confirmed paired-parallel-lattice instance after SE-135. The candidate refinement #10 promotes to formalization-ready.

Cluster A (D.5 ordinal-axis), four-activity ordinal lattice. The four activities (Establish / Plan / Perform / Evaluate) admit a temporal-precedence partial order (Establish first, Plan second, Perform third, Evaluate continuous-or-fourth). Cluster A D.5 sub-form gains a sixth load-bearing instance (after SE-160, SE-164's two co-located lattices, SE-116 Resilience, SE-071 SoS).

Cluster E (institutional ground, Doc 571), three-carrier robustness instance. PSM, GQM, ISO/IEC/IEEE 15939 are three independent carriers of the same measurement discipline. SE-039 §VII.7 reported three-carrier robustness as load-bearing at three SE-internal instances (SE-063 Measurement first read, SE-112 System Security, SE-114 IM); SE-167 reads the Measurement page directly and reaffirms the three-carrier instance there. The §X.5 three-carrier sub-form is now load-bearing at four SE-internal readings.

Cluster H (hypostatic boundary, Doc 372), four-pitfall teaching cluster. Golden-measure (no universal measure across projects), single-pass (measurement is continuous), data-without-information-need (measurement requires decision-purpose), inappropriate-use (measurement should not evaluate individual performance). The four pitfalls are operational and procedural; they describe failure modes without metaphysical claims about what measurement IS. SE-039 §VII.6 noted this four-pitfall teaching cluster as a candidate Cluster H Appendix worked example. SE-167 reaffirms.

Cluster K (virtue constraints, Doc 314), V3-as-procedure-binding at the four-activity process and the inappropriate-use pitfall. The four-activity procedure exists because measurement-by-discretion exhibits rankism (the measurer ranks their preferred measure above the decision-maker's information need) and complacency (measurement-without-evaluation lets stale measures persist). The inappropriate-use pitfall ("not evaluating individual performance") is V3 explicitly: measurement that conflates capability evaluation with personal evaluation rankism-fails the practitioner. Two V3 sub-modes: procedure-binding and use-binding. Cluster K density grows.

Cluster F (pulverization, Doc 445), forward-pulverization at the leading-indicator rung. "Leading indicators provide visibility into expected project performance and potential future states" is forward-pulverization at the project-rung temporal magnitude (project-quarter to project-year). Cluster F gains a leading-indicator rung instance.

Cluster B (multi-keeper composition, Doc 604), measurement-keeper plus decision-maker-keeper coordination. The measurement engagement composes the measurement-keeper (provides four-activity discipline) and the decision-maker-keeper (provides information-need that defines the measures). Coordination-by-rung composition. Standard Cluster B reading.

V. Residuals

Paired-parallel-lattice sub-form load-bearing at two confirming instances. SE-135 MBSE (Properties × Criteria) and SE-167 Measurement (process × measure-type) are now two independent SEBoK readings of the same Cluster A twin-lattice sub-form. The sub-form is structurally distinct from D.5.2 two-axis (where one lattice has two axes); paired-parallel-lattice is two co-bound lattices at the same rung, each contributing its own dimension to the engagement.

Three-carrier robustness fourth instance reaffirms §X.5 sub-form. SE-167 confirms three-carrier at the Measurement page directly; the sub-form is load-bearing across four SE-internal readings.
